subject.title: Feature: Activity-aware run timeout (wall-clock timeout kills active multi-tool runs)

question: Should OpenClaw change core agent turns from one wall-clock agents.defaults.timeoutSeconds budget to an activity-aware idle timeout plus a hard ceiling, and should that introduce new config surface?
rationale: The current code proves the remaining behavior is real, but choosing idle-vs-hard-cap semantics and any new config/default migration changes core runtime policy and existing operator expectations.

options.title: Choose contract before merging slices
options.body: Keep this issue open as the product parent, decide the idle/hard-cap contract, then review narrower PRs such as timeout notices and subagent heartbeats against that contract.

options.title: Add explicit idle and max config
options.body: Introduce separate idle and maximum turn timeout settings with schema/docs/tests and any required doctor guidance, accepting the new configuration surface.

options.title: Limit to symptom fixes
options.body: Preserve the existing wall-clock contract, land only user-visible timeout notices or channel/subagent-specific mitigations, and close this broader direction after documenting that choice.

recommendation.title: Choose contract before merging slices
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the product parent, decide the idle/hard-cap contract, then review narrower PRs such as timeout notices and subagent heartbeats against that contract.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest current history on the shared agent timeout resolver and gateway abort semantics that this decision would change.
